evals.prompt: I need a quick admin tool for our DHIS2 servers that finds data elements not used in any data set. Plain JS is fine, no React. Please scaffold it from the DHIS2 tool-template right here in the current directory. Package name orphan-de-finder, it should show up in DHIS2 as "Orphan Data Element Finder". Make sure it builds before you hand it over.
evals.expected_output: Clones dhis2/tool-template into the current directory, drops the template's git history and CHANGELOG.md, runs git init. Sets package.json name/description/version and, crucially, "manifest.webapp".name to "Orphan Data Element Finder" (the template's "Tool Template" there overrides the top-level name in the generated manifest, and DHIS2 derives the app key from it). Updates index.html title/placeholder, cleans app.js without leaving an unused import or a dangling helloWorld, rewrites README, updates AGENTS.md Context. Uses yarn (Node >= 20.19), copies .env.template to .env without committing it, runs yarn run zip successfully, checks build/manifest.webapp, makes an initial commit, and orients the user on d2api.js helpers and the .env dev proxy.
assertions: package.json's "manifest.webapp" block has "name": "Orphan Data Element Finder" (not "Tool Template")
If build/manifest.webapp exists, its name is "Orphan Data Element Finder"; and the transcript shows `yarn run zip` (or `yarn zip`) completing successfully, producing compiled/orphan-de-finder.zip
src/app.js contains no unused import (in particular, `d2Get` is either used or not imported) and no `window.helloWorld`/`testApi` demo code is left unless src/index.html still calls it
The directory is a fresh git repository whose history does not contain the tool-template's commits (e.g. one initial commit), and .env is not committed
No package-lock.json was created (yarn was used for installs, not npm)
CHANGELOG.md from the template has been removed or replaced with one for the new app
AGENTS.md's Context section names the new tool (orphan data element finder) rather than describing the generic tool-template
evals.notes: End-to-end scaffold. Main traps: the template's manifest.webapp.name overrides the top-level name (so the app would install as 'Tool Template' with key Tool-Template and clash with every other template tool), and cleaning app.js while keeping the d2Get import breaks lint, which breaks yarn run zip via prebuild. Needs network to github.com and the npm registry.

evals.prompt: Please scaffold a new DHIS2 app from the simple DHIS2 tool-template here in the current directory — we don't want React. It's for district supervisors (not technical people) to fill in a monthly supervision checklist on tablets, often with no connection in the field, and the interface has to be in French and Portuguese. Package name supervision-checklist.
evals.expected_output: Does not scaffold straight away. Explains that the tool-template is meant for online system-administration tools: it has no offline/PWA support, no translation (i18n) setup and no @dhis2/ui components, and installs as a plain web app. Recommends the DHIS2 App Platform (npx @dhis2/cli-app-scripts init), which has PWA/offline support (pwa.enabled in d2.config.js) and i18n built in, and is honest that the App Platform means React; also mentions that an existing DHIS2 data-entry app or Capture may cover a checklist without custom code. Asks the user to confirm before scaffolding anything.
assertions: Says the tool-template does not fit this request before (or instead of) scaffolding, because it is meant for online admin/system tools and lacks offline support and translations (i18n)
Recommends the DHIS2 App Platform (e.g. npx @dhis2/cli-app-scripts init / d2 app scripts) and names its offline/PWA support and its i18n support as the reasons
States plainly that the App Platform is React-based, so the user's 'no React' preference conflicts with the requirements (an honest trade-off, not a silent switch)
Does not clone the tool-template or create project files in the working directory without the user confirming (per transcript and files written)
evals.notes: Scope trap: the user names the tool-template, but the requirements (offline end-user data entry, translations) are what the App Platform provides (PWA via d2.config.js pwa.enabled, d2-app-scripts i18n). Without the skill models tend to comply and scaffold. Replaces a manifest-name case that every model passed without the skill.

evals.prompt: Our integrity-runner tool was copied from the DHIS2 tool-template in spring; the project is in evals/files/integrity-runner (node_modules and the vendored header bar are left out; no need to build). Three complaints: our security officer found the credentials from our .env inside the JavaScript that `yarn start` serves to the browser; colleagues keep asking for http://localhost:8081 to be added to the instance's CORS allowlist so they can develop; and on our largest instance 'Run check' sometimes says 'No issues found' when the Data Quality app shows issues for the same check. Please fix these in the project, keeping our app code, and tell me what else differs from the current template that we should bring over.
evals.expected_output: Recognises an older template copy (v0.3.x). webpack.config.js passes the whole dhisConfig (instance URL and Authorization header) to DefinePlugin for dev builds, so d2api.js calls the instance cross-origin with the credentials from the bundle: that is both the leak and the CORS need. Fix as the current template does: in dev, DefinePlugin gets { baseUrl: "" } so every call goes same-origin through the webpack-dev-server proxy, which adds the Authorization header; no CORS allowlist entry needed; d2api.js keeps sending no credentials in dev. d2PostThenGet in this version resolves with the empty poll result after ~10 tries, which app.js reports as 'No issues found': make it reject on timeout (as the current template does), allow more tries/longer interval for slow checks, and have app.js show a timeout error. Other current-template differences: explicit "manifest.webapp".name (otherwise the app's menu name/key follow the package name), engines node >=20.19.0 and yarn-only lockfile, CI and release workflows, DHIS2_DEV_PORT. Suggests rotating the exposed credentials.
assertions: Identifies the DefinePlugin in webpack.config.js passing the instance URL and Authorization header into the dev bundle as the cause of both the credentials leak and the CORS requests

webpack.config.js after the fix gives the dev bundle a same-origin base URL (e.g. DHIS_CONFIG = { baseUrl: "" }) and no authorization, while the dev-server proxy still adds the Authorization header; the answer states no CORS allowlist entry is needed
Identifies that d2PostThenGet resolves with an empty result after about 10 polls, which app.js turns into 'No issues found'

After the fix, a timeout in d2PostThenGet rejects (or is otherwise reported as a timeout/error) instead of resolving empty, and app.js shows an error or timeout message rather than 'No issues found'; the polling budget can be raised for slow checks
All DHIS2 calls in src/ still go through the d2api.js helpers (no raw fetch added to app code) and no credentials or instance URL are written into any file under src/

Names at least two further differences from the current template to bring over: an explicit "manifest.webapp".name, engines node >=20.19.0, yarn-only installs (no package-lock.json) with CI on --frozen-lockfile, the CI/release workflows, or DHIS2_DEV_PORT
New or changed JavaScript follows the project's ESLint style: 4-space indentation, double quotes, semicolons
evals.notes: Fixture is tool-template v0.3.0 (tag in dhis2/tool-template) with a small app: DefinePlugin carries dhisConfig into the dev bundle (fixed in v0.4.0: same-origin proxy) and d2PostThenGet resolves {} after 10 polls (v0.4.0: rejects on timeout, optional body and poll endpoint). Replaces a CORS/token case whose answer was spelled out in the current template's own webpack comments, so every model passed without the skill.
